nodes.label:
New Kit Type
Needed
nodes.title: New Kit Type Needed
nodes.info: A mentor identifies a gap in the shelf, such as no kit yet existing for a sensor a new lesson calls for.

nodes.label: Select a Vendor
nodes.title: Kit Vendor Selection
nodes.info: Comparing suppliers before ordering, weighing unit price against shipping time, part-quality consistency between orders, and how closely the vendor's actual product matches the pin layout the kit's documentation assumes.

nodes.label: Compare Total Cost
nodes.title: Kit Cost Comparison
nodes.info: Looking past the sticker price to cost per session actually delivered: purchase price plus shipping and one-time tools, divided by how many working sessions the kit survives.

nodes.label:
Order 10
or More?
nodes.title: Kit Bulk Purchasing
nodes.info: Ordering several identical kits at once unlocks a lower per-unit price and, just as valuable, guarantees every unit shares the same hardware revision. Either answer continues to unboxing.

nodes.label: Unbox and Test
nodes.title: Kit Unboxing Procedure
nodes.info: The one-time ritual before a kit reaches a student: confirm every part on the packing slip is in the box, power on and test the core sensor or output with the code template, and assign the kit its identifier.

nodes.label:
Run Safety
Checklist
nodes.title: Kit Safety Checklist
nodes.info: A short printed list of electrical checks -- no exposed conductor touching another wire, no reversed polarity, every connector seated snugly -- run during unboxing and again after any repair.

nodes.label:
Write Documentation
Sheet
nodes.title: Kit Documentation Sheet
nodes.info: The single page filed with each kit that gathers everything a mentor needs to run its station without the person who built it: difficulty rating, wiring diagram, code template, and debugging guide.

nodes.label:
Draw Wiring
Diagram
nodes.title: Kit Wiring Diagram
nodes.info: A labelled diagram showing exactly which physical pin -- named by the label printed on the module, such as SDA, SCL, VCC, or GND -- connects to which Pico pin, drawn for the exact board revision in the bin.

nodes.label:
Save Code
Template
nodes.title: Kit Code Template
nodes.info: A short already-working starter program, typically five to fifteen lines, that reads the core sensor or drives the core output and prints a result. Meant to be run exactly as written before any student customises it.

nodes.label:
Store in
Labeled Bin
nodes.title: Kit Storage Bin
nodes.info: A dedicated labelled container, one per kit type, holding the kit and its documentation sheet together between sessions, labelled consistently across the shelf so any kit is identifiable at a glance.

nodes.label:
Loan Out for
a Session
nodes.title: Kit Loaner Program
nodes.info: A kit leaves its bin for a defined period, with the club tracking which kit is out, who has it, and when it is due back -- the same accountability a library applies to a borrowed book.

nodes.label:
In Use -
Stuck?
nodes.title: In Use - Stuck?
nodes.info: If a kit stops behaving as expected while in use, a mentor consults its debugging guide before assuming damage.

nodes.label:
Consult Debugging
Guide
nodes.title: Kit Debugging Guide
nodes.info: A short troubleshooting table attached to the documentation sheet, pairing a symptom with its most likely fix -- 'no numbers appear' paired with 'reseat the data pins' -- so a stuck mentor has a first place to look.

nodes.label: Kit Returned
nodes.title: Kit Return Process
nodes.info: Before a kit re-enters circulation its parts are counted against the documentation sheet's part list and its core function is quick-tested with the code template.

nodes.label:
Damage
Assessment
nodes.title: Kit Damage Assessment
nodes.info: The judgement a mentor makes about a returned kit: purely cosmetic, an easy fix like a bent pin, or a genuine failure needing a replacement part. It starts with the debugging guide's fixes rather than jumping to replacement.

nodes.label: Reuse As-Is
nodes.title: Kit Reuse Strategy
nodes.info: The default outcome for any kit that passes return and damage assessment cleanly: straight back into its labelled bin, unchanged, ready for the next session.

nodes.label:
Revise and
Upgrade
nodes.title: Kit Upgrade Path
nodes.info: A deliberate revision to the documentation sheet, code template, or hardware -- not because anything is broken, but because a better approach has become clear. It sends the kit back through documentation.

nodes.label:
Retire and
Salvage Parts
nodes.title: Retire and Salvage Parts
nodes.info: A kit with unsafe or unrepairable damage is retired. Still-good parts, such as a working Pico or jumper wires, are salvaged into other kits' bins rather than thrown away.
